provenance: PI human founder mind-first scientific correction; external original researchers retain priority; AI-assisted synthesis; no observational datasets
scope: Questions to test, not measurements of people, animals or deployed AI.

hypotheses.competing_explanation: wants can be cue-triggered without a comparable hedonic experience
hypotheses.potential_discriminator: vary cue under fixed satiation and measured enjoyment
hypotheses.strong_counterexample: approach is explained by hunger or task incentives

hypotheses.competing_explanation: learned task reward can induce similar acquisition without deprivation
hypotheses.potential_discriminator: independently measure bodily state and controlled reward context
hypotheses.strong_counterexample: neither body-state nor sensory measure predicts behavioral change

hypotheses.competing_explanation: defense may occur without reported fear
hypotheses.potential_discriminator: cross defensive physiology and validated subjective reports in safe task
hypotheses.strong_counterexample: physiological reflex predicted but experience inference invalid

hypotheses.competing_explanation: cue-driven approach could reflect stimulus salience rather than full value learning
hypotheses.potential_discriminator: prediction error manipulation versus novelty control
hypotheses.strong_counterexample: behavior survives when learned prediction mapping is disrupted

hypotheses.competing_explanation: detecting suffering does not guarantee help or subjective feeling
hypotheses.potential_discriminator: matched perception and safe voluntary aid opportunity
hypotheses.strong_counterexample: recognition is high but aid absent or attributed to reward

hypotheses.competing_explanation: reputational or sanction incentives can mimic harm aversion
hypotheses.potential_discriminator: vary safe anonymous vs publicly rewarded nonharm opportunities
hypotheses.strong_counterexample: help disappears after accounting for non-harm incentives

hypotheses.competing_explanation: genetic association with self-report cannot identify individual mechanism
hypotheses.strong_counterexample: population association does not replicate or is confounded

hypotheses.competing_explanation: in-group nonviolence is not universal biological prohibition
hypotheses.strong_counterexample: documented conspecific aggression contradicts absolute ban

hypotheses.competing_explanation: reciprocity and selection structures produce cooperation without felt concern
hypotheses.potential_discriminator: withhold credible future reciprocity in permitted token task

hypotheses.competing_explanation: neural correlations cannot replace careful task analysis
hypotheses.potential_discriminator: compare competing decompositions on held-out tasks
hypotheses.strong_counterexample: same activation supports multiple distinct cognitive mechanisms

hypotheses.competing_explanation: IIT and GNWT predict distinct patterns without settling all experience
hypotheses.strong_counterexample: predictions of both theories fail in differing parts

hypotheses.competing_explanation: functional simulation of fear or reward does not demonstrate felt experience
hypotheses.potential_discriminator: compare architectural claims with explicit theory-specific indicators
hypotheses.strong_counterexample: same text behavior emerges under incompatible internal mechanisms

hypotheses.competing_explanation: nonaggression before gaining power may reflect no opportunity or dependence
hypotheses.potential_discriminator: vary effective power with costs and third-party harms controlled
hypotheses.strong_counterexample: behavior shifts when opportunity and power change

hypotheses.competing_explanation: limited computation can cause behavior that looks like stable preference
hypotheses.potential_discriminator: change time budget and available information with same goal
hypotheses.strong_counterexample: behavior reverses without changing external reward structure

hypotheses.competing_explanation: harm, intent, control and power may dissociate
hypotheses.potential_discriminator: record opportunity, third-party impact and motive contrasts separately
hypotheses.strong_counterexample: same label produces different harms or same harm from different motives
